planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Pierce is suited to zones 10-12 and sheltered zone 9b microclimates. Hand-pollination with a small brush is strongly recommended for reliable fruit set.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in zones 10-12; Pierce is a California-selected cherimoya cultivar valued for its smooth-skinned, relatively small-to-medium fruit that ripens later in the season than many other named selections, helping extend the cherimoya harvest window into winter. The white, custardy flesh is very sweet with the classic pineapple-banana-vanilla flavor typical of good cherimoya, and the fruit's smaller size makes it convenient for single-serving eating. Like all cherimoya, hand-pollination by transferring pollen from freshly opened male-phase flowers to receptive female-phase flowers with a small brush in the morning greatly improves fruit set, since the flowers' timing rarely allows a single flower to self-pollinate and natural pollinators are scarce outside the tree's native Andean range. Grafted Pierce trees begin bearing within two to four years and need protection from frost while young.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; Booth is a Florida-selected cultivar suited to zones 10-12 and sheltered zone 9b microclimates. Hand-pollination with a small brush is strongly recommended for reliable fruit set.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in zones 10-12; Booth is a long-established Florida cherimoya selection prized for reliable production and good-sized, conical, mildly ribbed fruit with rich, sweet, custardy white flesh and the classic tropical flavor blend of pineapple, banana, and vanilla. It has a reputation as one of the more dependable croppers among named cherimoya cultivars in Florida's warm, humid subtropical conditions, which can otherwise be a challenging environment for a species that prefers the cooler, drier climate of its Andean homeland. As with all cherimoya, hand-pollinate by transferring pollen from freshly opened male-phase flowers to receptive female-phase flowers with a small brush in the morning hours, since the flowers' protogynous timing makes natural self-pollination unreliable. Grafted trees bear within two to four years; protect young trees from frost and give them consistent moisture during fruit development.

planting.note: Plant grafted or container-grown trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Kampong Mauve is a distinctive pink-blushed sugar apple suited to zones 10-11 and warm, sheltered zone 9b sites, with no cold tolerance to speak of.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun in a warm, frost-free site; Kampong Mauve is a striking sugar apple selection with a distinctive dusty pink-to-mauve blush over its bumpy, segmented skin, standing out visually from the typical pale green sugar apple, while the sweet, creamy, custard-textured white flesh inside is classic sugar apple in flavor and texture. It is more cold-sensitive than cherimoya or atemoya and needs consistently warm, essentially tropical conditions to thrive, making it best suited to south Florida, south Texas, and similarly frost-free zones, or container culture that can be moved under cover in cooler areas. Hand-pollination with a small brush, transferring pollen between flowers in the evening or early morning when they are receptive, significantly improves fruit set in home garden settings where the tree's natural beetle pollinators may be scarce. Harvest when the segments on the fruit begin to separate slightly and the fruit softens, and eat promptly since ripe sugar apples do not store well.
